summary: [standards] Adequacy of the proof for the 14 `_UNAVAILABLE` codes (481ea88d): the committed tests only drive the pure helpers (`brief_code(&eio())`, `config_error(text-with-EIO)`, ...) and a few mapping fns on constructed errors, so they prove the classification but not that each call site routes its read error through the helper. I closed that gap by hand with real calls: a DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES shim (outside the repo, /Volumes/External/tmp/rev-refusals-b/eio) that returns EIO from open() on a path pattern, for the real debug `canon`: BRIEF_UNAVAILABLE (brief show, brief check), CONFIG_UNAVAILABLE (inventory sync), POLICY_UNAVAILABLE (policy approve), HOOKS_FILE_UNAVAILABLE (gate install-hooks), ADAPTER_FILE_UNAVAILABLE (adapter validate), RETENTION_TIERS_UNAVAILABLE (export), EVIDENCE_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE (--artifact and --report), REVIEW_ARTIFACT_UNAVAILABLE (review scenario --artifact), DISPATCH_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE (dispatch end), REPO_UNAVAILABLE (subject show): all exit 2, retryable true, no data. Not driven (a directory read, a mkdir or a strategy store needed): SPEC_ROOT, MIGRATION, PLAN_CORPUS, POLICY_APPROVAL, STRATEGY_SIGNATURE, DISPATCH_RUN and DISPATCH_DIFF_RECORDS. Verdict: adequate for the classification (pure, exhaustive over kinds), not by itself for the wiring; the wiring holds for the ten driven; a committed `DYLD`/LD_PRELOAD-free seam (like CANON_TEST_INDEX_LOCK_WAIT_MS, debug-only) that makes one read fail with EIO would let a test drive the other seven. Related: `EVIDENCE_BINDING_STALE` and `REVIEW_ARTIFACT_STALE` are a race between two reads of one file and are proved only by a unit test of the mapping on a constructed `ArtifactStoreError::Changed`; accepted, since the scenario text now says so.
